1. [blocking, issue-impact, high] [init.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/commands/init.rs:371) does not fully Git-escape an arbitrary nested `JIT_DATA_DIR`: it escapes only space, `#`, and `!`, converts a literal backslash to `/`, and leaves glob metacharacters such as `*`, `?`, and `[` active. Eligible init can therefore publish a merge rule that matches the wrong paths or fails to match its selected data root, violating the required literal Git-escaped claim. Git attributes uses `.gitignore` pattern semantics, including backslash escaping. [Git documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitattributes/2.17.0.html)

2. [blocking, issue-impact, medium] [main.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/main.rs:2057) exposes only `created_paths` and `modified_paths`; it never emits the typed attributes disposition. `not_applicable` and eligible-but-`unchanged` are therefore indistinguishable to CLI/JSON consumers, despite the required four-state Git-optional attributes contract. This also prevents consumers from observing Git-free operation under [@/charter/D-4](https://example.invalid/).
